name: Finding Adjacent Duplicates in a Sequence of Numbers
description: Construct a program that checks whether a sequence of numbers, entered one at a time, contains adjacent duplicates. The user enters -1 to indicate the end of the input.\nFor example, 4 is a duplicate in the sequence of numbers 1, 3, 4, 4, -1.

comments.content: We prompt the user to enter the numbers separated by spaces or new line. The user can enter -1 to quit.
We need to read and process the values that user enters. To read the input values from user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.

Note that, unless specified otherwise, a Scanner object assumes that whitespace characters (space characters, tabs, and new lines) are used to separate the input values from each other.
We read the first number that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the input by calling the nextDouble() method because the input could have a decimal point.
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid double value.

We need to repeat receiving the numbers from the user as long as the user enters a number that is different from -1. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the input number is different from -1.
The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user enters a number that is different from -1. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to false, that is when the user enters -1.
We store the number that the user entered in a variable called previous because we want to later compare it with the next number that user will enter to check if they are adjacent duplicate.

We need to read the next number that the user enters. The call to nextDouble() method returns the next number that the user enters. Note that if the input consists of a sequence of numbers separated by spaces or new line, each call to nextDouble() method would return the next number in the sequence.
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid double value.
We check whether the number that the user entered is the duplicate of the previous number that the user entered. To determine if the two numbers are duplicate we need to test whether they are equal.
If the number that the user entered is equal to the previous number that was entered, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
This statement prints the duplicate number to the default standard output stream. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the variable.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.
